Summary: Bernard records boarding on 9 April and leaving Sydney on Queen Elizabeth on Good Friday, 11 April.
The two voyage accounts give arrival on 16 April and departure on 19 April. They do not record a visit ashore.
Between the Fremantle and Ceylon entries, Bernard notes ten minutes’ silence for Anzac Day and the burial of a crew member at sea.
Qualification: No position is given. The text does not supply a separate numerical date for the burial; no point has been interpolated along the route.

Summary: He describes a green, pretty harbour, arriving at 6:30 am on 26 April and leaving at 4 pm on 27 April. He was not allowed ashore.
Qualification: The diary spells the port TRINCOMILEE. Trincomalee is the map identification; Ceylon is the period name used in the diary.

Summary: A brief pencil entry mentions Q E and Q M travelling together. The speed and following sea description are uncertain.
Qualification: The notebook provides no position. Its tentative speed has not been used to calculate distance or fill a ship’s track.

Summary: The ink account records unnamed land and a strange ship. The land has not been identified from an expected shipping route.
Qualification: The year follows from the surrounding 1941 voyage entries.

Summary: Aden is recorded at about 9 pm local time. The verb is “Passed”; the diary does not describe docking or going ashore.
Qualification: The pin locates Aden as a reference point. It does not mark the ship’s position.

Summary: The pencil and ink accounts both place arrival on 3 May. Bernard describes ships at anchor and the entrance to the Suez Canal. His own disembarkation follows on 6 May.
Qualification: Nearby wording about Saturday, Sunday and an inserted “4th” is ambiguous. A much fainter inside-cover note reads Arrived [Suez?] [7/5/41?], with Gaza an alternative place reading. The map follows the repeated clear 3 May arrival.

Summary: Bernard records disembarking at 6 am and transferring to a smaller ship for the canal journey to Kantara.
Qualification: The smaller vessel’s name remains [Euphthopea?] in one account and [Euthopea?] in the other. The separate timetable on photograph 0912 corroborates the date without naming the port.

Summary: He records arriving about 4 pm on 6 May, eating sausages, potatoes and peas, and boarding a train at 5:30 am on 7 May for Gaza.
Qualification: The preceding passage names Kantara East as the expected entraining point; the arrival sentences say El Kantara or Kantara.

Summary: Romani appears among the places passed on the train journey from Kantara towards Gaza.
Qualification: The date is carried from the surrounding 7 May railway entry. A named passing place does not establish a stop or time there.

Summary: The same railway passage names El Erich. The companion map identifies this as the El Arish area, retaining the diary’s spelling in the evidence.
Qualification: This is a geographical identification, not a correction to the faithful transcription. No arrival time is recorded.

Summary: The ink journey account records arrival at Gaza about 3 pm after the train journey.
Qualification: Kilo 89 is separately recorded on the same date. The notebook does not describe the connection between the Gaza arrival and the camp.

Summary: The tent-list page records arrival at Kilo 89 on 7 May and departure on 17 May. The movement note says he left to join 3rd Btn at JULIUS.
Qualification: Australian War Memorial captions associate Kilo 89 with Gaza Ridge. An exact camp position has not been established here, so it stays in the timeline without a pin.

Summary: One page records arrival at the unit at Julis, [Gellibrand?] lines. Another says he left Kilo 89 to join 3rd Btn at JULIUS.
Qualification: Archive sources associate Gellibrand with the historical Julis camp near the Gaza–Tel Aviv road. The camp’s precise position is not asserted; the handwriting’s [Gellibrand?] remains tentative.

Summary: The entry records leaving for Rehovot, 7 AGH, on 25 May.
Qualification: The reading copy identifies Rehovot and 7 AGH from the handwriting and the hospital record.

Summary: A march-in note names 1st Aust Corps Guard Btn and 16 ITB Special wing, followed by June 12 and an order reference.
Qualification: 1941 is inferred from surrounding notes. June 12 may relate to the event or the cited order; the entry does not state a location.

Summary: A page holds a memorial sketch and a small cemetery plan. The date beside the lower drawing is tentatively read [22/6/41?].
Qualification: The date and an actual visit are not securely established. This is shown as a notebook record, separate from the names page whose heading has a disputed June/September date. The pin indicates Gaza generally, not a verified drawing viewpoint.

Summary: A pencil line names Gaza Ridge and A.A.P.D., with the date 20 July.
Qualification: The final word remains uncertain. See the reading-copy revision ledger.

Summary: The notebook records a funeral cortege from Gaza hospital, of 9th Battalion.
Qualification: Gaza and cortege were clarified on renewed image review.

Summary: A later note records leaving port [Tewfic?] on 4 August, followed by HMT PP.
Qualification: No destination is recorded. HMT PP has not been expanded into a ship name, and the intervening movements have not been reconstructed.

Summary: A short note among addresses has Saturday inserted above Sunday, with 9/10 Aug 1941 and At [rom Catholic?].
Qualification: Neither a location nor the note’s purpose is established. Nearby addresses have not been turned into travel stops.

Summary: A heading beginning Gaza introduces names, units and earlier dates, apparently memorial or grave information. Its month may be June or September.
Qualification: The date is transcribed [23/9/41?], with 23/6/41 a plausible alternative. The heading does not explicitly record arrival or a cemetery visit. Dates from 1917–1918 concern the listed names. This record is excluded from month-specific ordering.

Summary: A pencil gateway frames a path, grave markers and a cross. The inscription above names Jerusalem War Cemetery.
Qualification: There is no visit date. The 1914–1918 wording belongs to the inscription. This reference place is not connected into the dated travel route.

Summary: A simple pencil outline is labelled SUEZ and Port Tewfic. The port is also named in the dated voyage entries.
Qualification: Those other entries do not date the sketch. No particular mountain, coast or viewpoint has been assigned to the outline.
